{{Short description|Kra language spoken in China}} {{Distinguish|Mulam language}} {{Infobox language | name = Mulao | states = China | region = [[Guizhou]] | extinct = 2010s | ref = e25 | familycolor = Tai–Kadai | fam2 = [[Kra languages|Kra]] | fam3 = Ge–Chi | fam4 = [[Gelao languages|Gelao]] | script = | iso3 = giu | glotto = gela1264 | glottorefname = Gelao Mulao }} '''Mulao''' ({{Lang-zh|s=木佬语|t=木佬語|p=Mùlǎoyǔ}}), also known as '''Ayo''',{{Cite web|title=Mulao|url=http://www.endangeredlanguages.com/lang/10586|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820052636/http://www.endangeredlanguages.com/lang/10586|archive-date=2020-08-20|access-date=2021-08-19|website=[[Endangered Languages Project]]|language=en}} is a possibly extinct [[Kra languages|Kra]] language spoken in [[Guizhou]], China.{{Cite web|title=UNESCO Atlas of the World's Languages in danger|url=http://www.unesco.org/languages-atlas/en/atlasmap/language-id-2422.html|access-date=2021-08-19|website=www.unesco.org}}{{Cite web|last=Yang|first=Cathryn|date=2011-05-18|title=ISO 639-3 Registration Authority: Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3|url=https://iso639-3.sil.org/sites/iso639-3/files/change_requests/2011/2011-053_giu.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211220725/https://iso639-3.sil.org/sites/iso639-3/files/change_requests/2011/2011-053_giu.pdf|archive-date=2019-12-11|access-date=2021-08-19|publisher=[[SIL International]]}} Spoken in [[Longli County]] and [[Majiang County]] in [[Guizhou]], it is estimated that the language may be extinct or have only have a few living speakers. As of 2011, there are no newspapers, radio programs, or television broadcasts in the language, and it is not recognized by the government, nor taught in schools. Mulao speakers are classified as [[Gelao people]] by the [[government of China]], but Mulao speakers do not understand the [[Gelao languages]]. It is closely related to [[A'ou language|A'ou]].Li Jinfang [李锦芳]. 2006. ''Studies on endangered languages in the Southwest China'' [西南地区濒危语言调查研究]. Beijing: Minzu University [中央民族大学出版社].Zhou Guoyan 周国炎. 2004. ''Gelaozu muyu shengtai yanjiu 仡佬族母語生态硏究 (Studies on the linguistic ecology of the Gelao people)''. Beijing: Ethnic Publishing House 民族出版社. ==Demographics== The Mulao number 28,000 people, and are distributed in [[Majiang County|Majiang]], [[Kaili City|Kaili]], [[Huangping County|Huangping]], [[Duyun]], [[Weng'an County|Weng'an]], [[Fuquan, Guizhou|Fuquan]], and other [[Counties of China|counties]] of southeastern Guizhou. The Mulao of Xuanwei and Jidong villages refer to themselves as the ''Mu'', and in Longli village ({{Lang-zh|c=龙里寨|labels=no}}) they call themselves ''{{IPA|qa24 ɣo53}}''. Luo (1997) describes the two Mulao varieties of ''{{IPA|qa24 o53}}'' (''{{IPA|qa24 ɣo53}}'') in Majiang County and ''{{IPA|lei35 wo33}}'' in Kaili City. One dialect is represented by the datapoints of Bamaozhai ({{Lang-zh|c=巴茅寨|labels=no}}) and Madizhai ({{Lang-zh|c=马碲寨|labels=no}}) of Xuanwei District ({{Lang-zh|c=宣威区|labels=no}}), Majiang County (Luo 1997:105, 115), and the other by Bailazhai ({{Lang-zh|c=白腊寨|labels=no}}), {{Interlanguage link|Lushan, Kaili|lt=Lushan|zh|炉山镇 (凯里市)}} ({{Lang-zh|c=炉山镇|labels=no}}), Kaili City (Luo 1997:189); the latter is also spoken in Dafengdong ({{Lang-zh|c=大风洞|labels=no}}), Pingliang ({{Lang-zh|c=平良|labels=no}}), and Chong'anjiang ({{Lang-zh|c=重安江|labels=no}}). The last speaker in Longli County was recorded by Bo Wenze (2003). ==Documentation== Monographs of Mulao include Bo (2003)Bo, Wenze 薄文泽. 2003. ''Mulaoyu yanjiu (A Study of Mulao)'' [木佬语硏究]. Beijing: Central University for Nationalities Publishing House [中央民族大学出版社]. and Luo (1997).Luo, Shiqing [罗世庆]. 1997. ''The ethnic Mulao of Guizhou'' [贵州仫佬族]. Guiyang: Guizhou People's Press [贵州民族出版社]. A word list is also given in Zhang (1993).Zhang, Jimin 张済民. 1993. ''Gelaoyu yanjiu 仡佬语研究 (A study of Gelao)''.
